subject: NWEA MAP Growth Assessment Overview
overview: District administrators presented an overview of the NWEA MAP growth assessment tool, explaining how computer-adaptive testing measures student progress throughout the year. The session detailed how to interpret student reports and how the data informs classroom instruction and personalized learning.

items.title: Introduction to NWEA MAP
items.summary: Presenters defined the Northwest Evaluation Association (NWEA) and the Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) assessment as a norm-based tool used to track student growth.

items.title: Computer Adaptive Testing Mechanics
items.summary: The assessment was described as a computer-adaptive test that adjusts question difficulty based on student performance to identify their specific level of academic knowledge.

items.title: RIT Scores and Testing Timeline
items.summary: Staff explained the Roche unit (RIT) scoring system and outlined the three-part annual testing window for elementary, middle, and high school students.

items.title: Growth Mindset Philosophy
items.summary: The district emphasized using test data to propel students forward by focusing on strengths and weaknesses rather than treating the score as a fixed measure of ability.

items.title: Practice Test Demonstration
items.summary: Administrators demonstrated the student interface and built-in accessibility features, including highlighters, line readers, and digital notepads.

items.title: Interpretation of Family Reports
items.summary: Presenters walked through a sample report, explaining color-coded percentile rankings and how plot graphs track individual achievement versus national norms over time.

items.title: MCAS Correlation and Q&A
items.summary: The presentation noted that MAP scores include a projected MCAS performance level and concluded by addressing parent questions about report details.
